newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuanian currency board to stay - minister.
newsitem.headline: Lithuanian currency board to stay - minister.

text.p: Lithuania is unlikely to scrap soon the currency board system by which it keeps its litas unit stable, Finance Minister Algimantas Krizhinauskas said Thursday.
The litas is currently pegged at four to one dollar via the currency board, which exactly backs the amount of litas in circulation with dollars in the central bank's reserves.
"There is no doubt that before October 1, 1997, nothing will change," Krizhinauskas told a news conference.
He noted that Lithuania promised the International Monetary Fund (IMF) it would preserve the currency board until that date.
"Even afterwards I am sure the litas rate will not change as no government will be able to afford the luxury of devaluing it," he added.
Opposition politicians and some business have called for the currency to be devalued as they say the current rate is harming Lithuanian exporters.
But the government and Western institutions say that keeping the litas stable has increased Lithuania's international credibility and helped to fight inflation.
Krizhinauskas also said it would take a long time for the central bank to work out in which way it would restore its functions and what powers it would need.
